newsitem.title: MEXICO: Indians burn election stations in Mexican state.
newsitem.headline: Indians burn election stations in Mexican state.

text.p: Mobs of angry Mexican Indians burned four polling stations in the troubled southern state of Chiapas during mid-term elections on Sunday, eyewitnesses said.

Hundreds of supporters of the Mayan Zapatista rebels also tore down voting booths and burned ballots in two villages in the area and dozens of other Indians blocked local highways, the witnesses added.

Zapatista rebels in the state called last week for an election boycott to protest a lack of progress in stalled peace talks between the government and the guerrillas, who launched an uprising for Indian rights and democracy on New Years Day 1994.
Rebel leader Subcommander Marcos said the boycott would be "a protest against militarization and the atmosphere of civil war promoted by federal and local governments."
Zapatista supporters ransacked the polling stations in the villages of San Andres Larrainzar and Tzuben, both remote towns about 400 miles (660 km) southeast of Mexico City.

Federal election officials said they decided not to install some 23 polling stations in so-called Zapatista territory, a swath of land in the state controlled by rebels. Zapatista supporters said they planned to prevent another 20 polling stations from opening outside the area.
